item.title: Abby Holliday & Charli Adams — Fri Aug 7, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: Women That Rock Summer Tour w/ Abby Holliday & Charli Adams and Eliza Harrison Smith Friday August 7th \*\*\* Nashville based singer-songwriter, Abby Holliday, has been writing songs for as long as she can recall. The 25-year-old burgeoning young artist is best known for exploring serious themes without taking herself too seriously. Bearing resemblance to the sonic qualities of female icons Phoebe Bridgers and Japanese House, Holliday’s songwriting is a unique intersection of sad vibes, introspective lyricism, and modern pop-sensibility. Holliday attempts to examine her external world as a skeptic — not a cynic — and her internal world with honesty — not cruelty. By way of the journal entries that she calls her songs, Holliday invites others to do the very same. \*\*\* Hailing from Alabama, Charli Adams is a singer-songwriter who found her musical calling at a young age. June McDoom — Fri Oct 23, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoomʼs debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own. She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Smidley — Mon Oct 26, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: Instead of letting Smidley devolve into a desperate vanity project or walking away from music entirely, Conor Murphy is immersing himself in his own potential. In the past ten years, Murphy the person and Smidley the band have come to exist beyond the mere creative overflow left unexplored in his work with Foxing. It’s a common and often perfunctory dilemma for an artist coming from a recently defunct ensemble. Through his own growth in and out of Smidley, though, art and life itself have entered into an ongoing cycle of redefinition. This redefinition isn’t a destination, but a new pathway paved by Murphy’s gratitude for and security in the artist, husband, and man that he’s become. Smidley’s third album, Murphy Horse, soundtracks this journey. The ephemerality of the present, and any confidence in it, is often simultaneously an artist’s greatest fear and motivation. Jackie Evans — Mon Nov 2, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description:
For New York-based singer/songwriter Jackie Evans, music has always been the only option, but Evans only began releasing songs under her own name last year. Her style, often likened to the timeless writing of Carole King, Billy Joel and Sara Bareilles is, in part, the byproduct of years spent taking requests at piano bars. As a gigging musician, Evans has tried it all; from playing standards on cruise ships, to performing at theme parks and majoring in theater. The ease and confidence she carries in live performance has caught the attention of other musicians, leading to collaborations with Vulfpeck, and support slots on tour with Lake Street Dive and Jensen McRae.
Source: Songbyrd
